doc.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024

title: Integrity, gatekeepers and players recording tracks at home
summary: Asked about 'integrity', Rowe says there are fewer gatekeepers, so young players should have their work vetted before releasing it online.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Could I zone in on a word you used, “integrity.” What did you mean by that? I was interested to learn when I interviewed Randy Brecker that much of what he does now is he stays at home and people send him tracks and he plays various solos on them.
I’m not saying that has something to do with integrity but it is an eye opener.

Um hum. Yeah. It’s definitely a shift. I’ve been hearing that more and more from players, that that’s a big part of what they do now. And yeah, I mean I think in order to be one of those players that’s going to have those tracks sent to them, like a Randy Brecker or Marshall Gilkes or whoever it might be, you have to be at the very top of your game still. So I mean I think when I was using the word “integrity” I was thinking about the fact that there’s not as many gatekeepers out there in terms of putting your music out. I mean there’s a lot of very — I’ll just try to be kind and say marginal — you know things that younger players are now able to put out and it’s not because they’re not talented it’s just because they’re you know young, and they can just thrown anything out on the web that they want to and you know I think all of us are trying to encourage our younger players to, you know, make sure that they’re getting their material vetted by older players and teachers and people that have an interest in their careers, and just to make sure it’s of the highest quality possible, since it is so easy to record something in your bedroom, you

know layer it up and send it out and there it goes and you know nobody over the age of 18 has heard it before, it’s just heading out there. You know so I think that’s what I meant, just to make sure that even though there might be avenues — a lot more avenues open to putting your music out there, to make sure you’re being very critical of yourself and you know, attending to the best practices for learning to play, learning to compose.
